title: Editing a Curve in a certain way consistently freezes the engine
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: Godot 4.5, Godot 4.4 ### System information Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8097) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12400F (12 threads) - 15.81 GiB memory ### Issue description Bringing two points too closely to each other in a Curve consistently crashes the engine if done so while holding Crtl. The issue was ***NOT*** replicable without holding Crtl. This issue also was not replicable if the curve's domain range was smaller than is indicated below in the steps section (as per my testing anyway). https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/029201f9-7ce6-4829-aa13-c18b1624f3a2 I know that the video shows me using some plugins, but I have tested this in a different project without any plugins, and it still crashed in more or less the same way. ~The issue isn't perfectly replicable from what I can tell. It seems that the point at which it triggers the crash is a bit off from project and scene to another.~ (Struck thru text is no longer relevant after some testing as far as I can tell, but since I'm not 100% sure, I'll keep it there just in case) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a Node. 2. Create a script and attach it to said Node. 3. Export a variable of type **Curve**. 4. Set the "min domain" to [-400], and the "max domain" to [0]. 5. Set the "min value" to [-4], and the "max value" to [4]. 6. Place a point at the min domain (far left)*, and set it to the min value (bottom). 7. Place another point at [-120]* (domain). 8. And finally, place one at [-280, 4]*, then keep holding Ctrl and move this point to [-360, -4]. *Note: I was holding Ctrl the whole time while placing the points and moving them around the curve. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [CurveCrashTest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22726774/CurveCrashTest.zip)
